Abstract

Executive Summary of the Bidirectional Indian Sign Language and Kannada Translation System

Report Abstract (Page iii)
Project Abstract

Communication between Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) citizens who communicate using Indian Sign Language (ISL) and hearing individuals who speak Kannada remains a significant challenge across hospitals, banks, classrooms, and government offices in Karnataka. Existing automated sign language tools largely focus on one-way American Sign Language (ASL) to English translation or depend on specialized wearable gloves and cloud-based raw video processing.

This project develops Silent Bridge, a browser-executable, bidirectional translation system connecting Indian Sign Language and Kannada. In the forward path (ISL to Kannada), webcam video is processed locally via MediaPipe Holistic to extract a 147-dimensional scale-invariant anatomical feature vector capturing dual 21-point hand skeletons, facial landmarks, and hand-to-face spatial anchors. A 3-state Hysteresis Motion Segmenter isolates continuous sign boundaries, and a hybrid Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Connectionist Temporal Classification (BiGRU-CTC) model classifies gestures via ONNX Runtime Web to synthesize grammatical Kannada text and speech. In the reverse path (Kannada to ISL), a rule-based Kannada morphological stemmer strips agglutinative suffixes, reorders clauses from Subject–Object–Verb (SOV) to ISL topological order, and drives a 60 FPS Three.js 3D humanoid avatar using a closed-form two-bone Analytic Inverse Kinematics (IK) solver with parabolic co-articulation trajectories.

Forward Path (ISL ➔ Kannada)
  • 30 FPS client-side holistic landmark extraction.
  • 147-D wrist-centered, shoulder-scaled encoding.
  • 3-state hysteresis continuous boundary detector.
  • Browser ONNX classification & Kannada TTS voice.
Reverse Path (Kannada ➔ ISL)
  • Unicode Kannada text & spoken microphone input.
  • 3-tier agglutinative suffix stripping rules.
  • SOV-to-ISL clause reordering engine.
  • 60 FPS 2-bone Analytic IK 3D signing avatar.
Datasets & Evaluation Scope
  • Harmonized Amrita-ISLR, INCLUDE & ISL-CSLTR.
  • 144 sign vocabulary classes & 187 phrases.
  • Evaluated on 314 real video streams.
  • Includes in-browser Few-Shot custom sign studio.

Introduction & Rationale for Topic Selection

Domain Context of Indian Sign Language (ISL) and Motivation for Selecting This Topic

Report Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1 (pp. 1–4)
1. Domain Introduction: Indian Sign Language (ISL)
  • Visual-Spatial Natural Language: Indian Sign Language (ISL) is a complete visual-gestural language with its own phonological, morphological, and syntactic structure independent of spoken languages.
  • Multi-Channel Articulation: Meaning in ISL is conveyed simultaneously through manual articulators (two-hand configuration, palm orientation, spatial location, and movement trajectory) and non-manual facial markers (eyebrow raise, mouth aperture, and head tilt).
  • Structural Divergence from Spoken Kannada: Spoken and written Kannada is an agglutinative Dravidian language with Subject–Object–Verb (SOV) order and rich case/tense suffixes, whereas ISL uses a Topic–Comment / Temporal-First syntactic structure without inflectional suffixes.
  • Demographic Context: Over 63 million individuals in India experience hearing or speech impairments (WHO / Census), including hundreds of thousands of citizens across Karnataka whose regional civic language is Kannada.
2. Why We Selected This Topic (Motivation)
  • Absence of Regional Kannada Sign Tools: Existing sign language datasets and recognition tools predominantly focus on American Sign Language (ASL) and English, leaving Kannada-speaking doctors, bank clerks, and families without accessible translation tools.
  • Critical Need in Healthcare & Public Desks: During outpatient hospital consultations, banking transactions, and railway inquiries, Deaf citizens struggle to communicate symptoms or requests when human interpreters are unavailable.
  • Need for Bidirectional Conversation: Real-world dialogue requires two-way translation—converting a Deaf person's signs into Kannada speech, and converting the hearing person's Kannada response back into visual sign language.
  • Need for Hardware-Free Privacy: Public service desks and clinics require a solution that operates on standard laptop webcams without expensive sensor gloves or uploading private patient videos to cloud servers.

Problem Statement & Project Objectives

Defining the Core Communication Barriers and Engineering Objectives

Report Ch. 1, Sec. 1.2–1.4 (pp. 5–8)
Problem Statement (Report Section 1.2)

Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) citizens in Karnataka face a severe two-way communication barrier when interacting with Kannada-speaking healthcare professionals, educators, and civic counter staff due to:

  • Acute Scarcity of Certified ISL Interpreters: With only ~350 certified interpreters nationwide, on-site interpretation is unavailable for everyday hospital triage, banking, and classroom interactions.
  • Technical Gaps in Existing Vision Systems: Current automated sign systems are largely unidirectional (Sign-to-English), sensitive to camera distance and background clutter, prone to false triggers during continuous signing, and lack reverse translation from agglutinative Kannada grammar into smooth 3D sign animation.
Project Objectives (Report Section 1.4)
Objective 1: Scale-Invariant Hand & Face Landmark Extraction
To design a privacy-preserving, browser-based feature extraction pipeline that captures two-hand skeletal joints and facial grammar landmarks normalized for camera seating distance.
Objective 2: Continuous Sign Segmentation & Classification
To develop a motion-hysteresis segmentation module and hybrid neural classifier capable of recognizing isolated and continuous Indian Sign Language gestures in real time.
Objective 3: Kannada SOV Morphological & Grammar Engine
To construct a bidirectional linguistic engine that synthesizes natural Kannada sentences from recognized ISL glosses and converts Kannada SOV input into ISL word order.
Objective 4: 3D Signing Avatar with Analytic Inverse Kinematics
To implement an interactive 3D humanoid avatar driven by closed-form two-bone inverse kinematics and smooth co-articulation trajectories for Kannada-to-ISL visualization.

Literature Survey

Review of Existing Sign Language Recognition & Avatar Synthesis Research Papers

Report Chapter 2 (pp. 9–17)
Table 2.1: Survey of Existing Research Papers and Identified Limitations
Author(s) & Year Methodology / Model Used Dataset / Modality Limitations & Research Gap Identified
Abhishek et al. (2020) Wearable flex & IMU sensor glove with SVM classifier Custom 30-sign hardware dataset Requires costly wired glove hardware (~Rs. 18,000); cannot capture facial grammar or non-manual expressions.
Koller et al. (2019) Deep CNN + Weakly Supervised HMM on raw RGB video RWTH-PHOENIX Weather (DGS) High GPU memory requirement; overfits to background lighting and signer clothing on unseen users.
Sridhar et al. (2020) Deep 3D-CNN / BiLSTM over raw video frames INCLUDE 263-Sign Isolated ISL Dataset Restricted to pre-trimmed isolated clips; lacks continuous stream boundary detection and regional language output.
Elakkiya & Natarajan (2021) Subunit sign modeling with 2D pose keypoints + LSTM ISL-CSLTR Sentence Corpus Fixed sliding windows cause boundary insertion errors during natural inter-sign pauses.
Wadhawan & Kumar (2021) CNN-based static & dynamic handshape classifier 35,000 static ISL alphabet/word images One-way recognition to English text only; omits non-manual facial cues and reverse sign animation.
Saunders et al. (2020) Progressive Transformers for skeletal pose generation PHOENIX14T German Sign Language Requires server-grade GPUs and lacks closed-form inverse kinematics, causing mid-sentence arm drops.

Feature Extraction Schema (147-D Hand, Face & Motion)

Anatomical Feature Vector Composition (Table 5.1) and Multi-Corpus Dataset Distribution

Report Ch. 5, Sec. 5.2 (pp. 35–38)
Table 5.1: 147-D Per-Frame & 441-D Window Feature Vector Schema
Feature Block Indices Dims Anatomical Representation & Normalization
Left Hand Skeleton [0 : 63] 63-D 21 joints × (x,y,z), wrist-centered & scaled by shoulder span St
Right Hand Skeleton [63 : 126] 63-D 21 joints × (x,y,z), wrist-centered & scaled by shoulder span St
Hand-to-Face Vectors [126 : 132] 6-D 3D displacement from Left & Right wrists to nose tip anchor
Facial Grammar Cues [132 : 143] 11-D Eyebrow raise, Mouth MAR, Eye EAR, and head pitch/yaw/roll
Bimanual & Velocity [143 : 147] 4-D Inter-wrist distance dLR, hand presence flags & wrist speed
Temporal Pooling [0 : 441] 441-D Mean (μ, 147-D) ⊕ Std Dev (σ, 147-D) ⊕ Velocity (Δ, 147-D)
Why These Features Are Extracted:
• Scale Invariance: Normalizing by inter-shoulder span St keeps feature magnitudes consistent across 0.5m–1.8m seating distances.
• Cranial Disambiguation: Hand-to-face vectors separate minimal-pair signs sharing identical handshapes near the forehead vs. chin.
Graph: Multi-Corpus Dataset Distribution (Fig. 5.2)
Three Harmonized ISL Corpora (Table 3.2):
• Amrita-ISLR: Clinical & daily isolated vocabulary
• INCLUDE: Multi-signer lexical categories
• ISL-CSLTR: Continuous sentence sign streams
• Total: 144 Sign Classes · 187 Phrases · 314 Video Streams

Module-Wise Implementation (How & Why)

Detailed Explanation of All Six System Modules and Their Functional Implementation

Report Chapter 6 (pp. 45–54)
Table 6.1: Implementation of All Core System Modules (How & Why)
Module Name HOW It Is Implemented WHY It Is Needed
1. Holistic Landmark Module Extracts 21 left-hand, 21 right-hand & 12 face points at 30 FPS via MediaPipe WASM. Eliminates background lighting noise and keeps webcam video private on device.
2. Hysteresis Motion Segmenter 3-state velocity FSM (IDLE ➔ SIGNING ➔ HOLD_PAUSE) with dual velocity gates. Prevents resting hand twitches from triggering false words and isolates strokes.
3. Hybrid ONNX Classifier Combines 441-D MLP + BiGRU-CTC temporal decoder exported to ONNX Runtime Web. Captures both static hand postures and temporal motion order in 4.6 ms on CPU.
4. Few-Shot Custom Sign Module In-browser Float32 2-layer MLP (441➔96➔C) trained with AdamW & 12× augmentation. Enables users to enroll new regional/medical signs from 3–5 clips in 45 seconds.
5. Kannada SOV Grammar Module 3-tier suffix stemmer & clause reorderer ([Time ➔ Subj ➔ Obj ➔ Verb ➔ Neg]). Maps agglutinative Kannada grammar to ISL order and synthesizes kn-IN voice.
6. 3D Avatar Analytic IK Module Closed-form 2-bone law-of-cosines Shoulder-Elbow-Wrist IK with parabolic arcs. Renders 144 signs at 60 FPS with chest guard and zero mid-sentence arm drops.

Key Observations from Comparative Testing (Sec. 7.3):
• Incorporating 21-D facial and hand-to-face features improved unseen-signer accuracy from 54.5% to 62.9%.

Conclusion & Future Work

Summary of Engineering Work Completed and Scope for Future Extensions

Report Chapter 8 (pp. 64–66)
1. Conclusion (Summary of Work Done — Sec. 8.1)
  • Bidirectional Translation Platform Built: Designed and implemented a browser-executable web application supporting both ISL-to-Kannada recognition and Kannada-to-3D Avatar sign synthesis.
  • 147-D Anatomical Landmark Extraction: Implemented local MediaPipe Holistic extraction of 147-D hand and facial features normalized by shoulder span, preserving complete user camera privacy.
  • Continuous Segmentation & Hybrid Model: Integrated a 3-state Hysteresis Motion Segmenter with a 441-D MLP and BiGRU-CTC classifier exported to ONNX Runtime Web (4.6 ms latency).
  • Kannada SOV Stemmer & 3D Analytic IK: Built a rule-based Kannada morphological stemmer, SOV-to-ISL clause reorderer, and a 60 FPS Three.js avatar with parabolic transition arcs.
  • Empirical Testing Completed: Tested across 314 real videos from Amrita-ISLR, INCLUDE, and ISL-CSLTR, recording 81.5% overall Top-1 accuracy and 76.5% on unseen signers.
2. Future Work (Scope for Enhancement — Sec. 8.2)
  • Vocabulary Expansion to 1,000+ Signs: Expand the dataset and active vocabulary to cover specialized medical triage, legal aid, and banking terminology across regional dialects.
  • Transformer & Diffusion Avatar Prosody: Incorporate spatio-temporal Transformer decoders for continuous finger-spelling and diffusion-based facial blendshapes for richer eyebrow and mouthing cues.
  • Multi-Language Dravidian Grammar Support: Extend the agglutinative SOV morphological stemmer and clause reordering rules to support Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam alongside Kannada.
  • Offline Mobile & Rural Kiosk Packaging: Package the WebAssembly inference pipeline as an offline Progressive Web App (PWA) for low-cost Android tablets in rural primary health centers.
